hook: The flute-playing soldier king who made Prussia a great power.

pages.x: Frederick was born in Berlin in 1712. His father, the soldier king Frederick William I, beat and humiliated him for loving music, French books and the flute, which he called unmanly.
At 18 he tried to run away to England with his friend Hans von Katte. They were caught. His father made Frederick watch from a prison window as Katte was beheaded.
He became king in 1740, and within months marched into the rich Austrian province of Silesia and took it. He spent most of the next 23 years at war to keep it.

In the Seven Years' War Prussia fought Austria, France and Russia at once, and Russian troops even took Berlin. Frederick, close to despair, was saved when the Russian empress died and her successor, a fan of his, made peace. Prussia kept Silesia.

At Potsdam he built a small summer palace, Sanssouci, "without worries". There he played the flute in evening concerts, wrote more than 100 flute sonatas, and invited Voltaire to stay. They quarrelled after three years.

He wanted his peasants to grow potatoes, but they would not. A story says he planted a royal potato field and had it guarded, so that people thought the potatoes must be precious, and stole them to plant. People still leave potatoes on his grave.

He called himself "the first servant of the state". He banned torture, let everyone worship as they wished, "for everyone must be saved in his own way", and started schools. He died in 1786 and asked to be buried beside his dogs.
Frederick turned Prussia into a great power, the core of the later German Empire, and became the model of an "enlightened" ruler: a philosopher king with absolute power.
pts: Made Prussia a great European power
A brilliant general in the Seven Years' War
Ended torture and allowed freedom of worship
